title: kernel-coalescing-and-memory-bank-conflict-diagnostics-may-2026
content:
Purpose and context:
Quick investigation notes on a regression observed in the 8-bit quantized attention kernel (attn_fwd_q8) where GPU throughput dropped ~20% on long-history chat loads. Suspect memory access pattern changes in a recent refactor (tensor layout -> blocked-by-16) introduced non-coalesced loads and increased shared memory bank conflicts in the reduction step. This doc collects Nsight traces, microbench ideas, hypotheses and immediate mitigations.

Summary of findings (short):
- End-to-end latency increase concentrated in a single kernel: attn_fwd_q8 (forward pass).
- Warp execution efficiency fell from ~91% -> ~67% for problematic inputs.
- Measured achieved occupancy for the kernel is ~0.45 on A100 (theoretical max with current block size ~0.937), suggesting SM underutilization despite many active warps.
- L2 transactions and serialize stalls increased (L2_TEX and EXEC_DEPENDENCY visible in Nsight timeline).
- Memory access trace shows strided accesses with 64B misaligned starts; likely caused by blocked-by-16 layout + embedding dim not multiple of 16.

Environment and commands run:
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100-SXM, CUDA 11.8 driver stack, nvml v470, nsight systems 2025.3.1.
- App build: serving-runtime @ commit 0b3e4f, attn quant branch attn-refactor-16block.
- Capture commands used (representative):
  - nsys profile -o traces/coalesce-run-2026-05-12 --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --sample=none --env="NSYS_MON_TRACE=1" --target-processes=all ./bin/serve_local --config tests/long_history.json
  - nvprof deprecated but used an older microbench: nvprof --metrics warp_execution_efficiency,inst_executed,branch_efficiency ./build/microbench/attn_memcheck
  - cuda-memcheck for invalid accesses in earlier iteration.

Key timeline observations (from Nsight .nsys-rep):
- Two hotspots around the same timestamp: attn_fwd_q8 kernel (duration ~12.2 ms) and a following kernel attn_softmax (duration ~2.1 ms). The long attn_fwd_q8 segment includes repeated memory copy bursts (async P2P) observed as memcpy nodes.
- Kernel internals: long gaps between warps launching; trace shows sequential micro-batches being serialized rather than overlapped. Stream use appears correct but kernel launch pacing varies.
- Stall reasons flagged: L2_TEX (elevated), EXEC_DEPENDENCY on some threadblocks, and MEMORY_THROUGHPUT_LIMIT.

Low-level metrics (sampled):
- attn_fwd_q8:
  - warp_execution_efficiency: 67%
  - sm_efficiency (approx): 48%
  - achieved_occupancy: 0.45
  - gld_transactions_per_request: 3.6 (expected ~1.0 for coalesced loads)
  - shared_load_bank_conflicts: high (per-block reduction shows 5+ conflicts on hot warps)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Layout change -> misaligned base pointers + blocking-by-16 causes per-warp strided loads that hit multiple cache lines => higher L2 traffic and uncoalesced requests.
2) Reduction code uses 32-bit indexing into shared memory but kernel was recompiled with 64-thread tiles; bank conflict pattern changed because bank mapping is different for 32-bit words vs 64-bit views.
3) Kernel launch configuration (blockDim.x) shifted during autotuning pass; for some sequence lengths the kernel uses block sizes that under-utilize SM resources, which combined with serial launches reduces occupancy.
4) cudaMemcpyAsync ordering: host->device prefetch stage sometimes stalls due to single stream device-side dependency; should use multiple streams / cudaMemcpyPeerAsync for P2P copies.

Repro steps and checks to isolate cause:
- Reproduce microbench with controlled tile sizes: build microbench that loads same memory pattern with varying alignment offsets 0..127 bytes, measure gld_transactions and warp_efficiency.
- Run nvprof/ncu on microbench with metrics: dram_read_transactions, l2_read_transactions, warp_execution_efficiency, shared_load_bank_conflicts.
- Add NVTX markers around memory layout conversion routines to ensure we can see when conversion happens relative to kernel dispatch.
- Run kernel with different blockDim.x (32,64,128,256) to observe achieved_occupancy and latency tradeoffs.
- Create small repro that toggles embedding_dim%16==0 vs !=0 to confirm coalescing sensitivity.

Quick mitigations tried (results):
- Restored old layout (pre-refactor) locally: latency returned to baseline. Conclusion: layout change is primary suspect.
- Forced __restrict__ pointers + aligned attribute (align(128)) on some buffers: improved gld_transaction count from 3.6 -> 1.4 and warp_efficiency up to ~82% in microbench, but full app still shows serialization likely due to leftover bank conflict in reduction.
- Slightly increased blockDim.x from 128 -> 256 lowered per-kernel latency but increased register pressure; achieved occupancy improved to ~0.6 but performance for short sequences degraded. So there’s a sequence-length-dependent sweet spot.

Open experiments and next steps:
- (A) Microbench matrix: for offsets in [0,16,32,48,64,80,96,112], run gld transaction measurement and bank conflict counters. Owner: Miguel. Target date: 2026-05-20.
- (B) Shared memory view alternative: test both 32-bit and 64-bit reductions (pack/unpack) to measure bank conflict delta. Owner: Hannah. Target date: 2026-05-22.
- (C) Autotuner sweep: include alignment-aware penalty term to avoid layouts that create heavy uncoalesced access. Owner: Ethan. Target date: 2026-05-28.
- (D) Short-term patch: revert layout change for production builds for sequence lengths > 1024 until we have robust quantized kernel. Owner: Aisha. Target date: 2026-05-19 (hotfix).

Longer term ideas:
- Introduce a lightweight runtime check that computes embedding_dim % warp_size and falls back to an alignment-correcting path at runtime (cheap and avoids recompile).
- Add a small instrumentation mode in release builds that emits per-kernel gld/l2 metrics to CloudMetrics for automatic regression detection (use sampling to limit overhead).
- Consider revisiting quantized kernel tiling to use vectorized loads (uint4/uint2) when alignment permits; add allocator hint API to satisfy 128B alignment for hot tensors.

Notes on measurement fidelity and cautions:
- Nsight can reorder reported events slightly vs on-device behavior (timestamps relative to host). Use device-side timers (clock64) inside microbench to confirm absolute times if uncertain.
- nvprof and ncu sometimes disagree on conflict counters; treat trends as signal rather than absolute ground truth.
- When increasing blockDim.x we saw register spill warnings; always watch max registers per thread to avoid spilling into local memory which will confound results.

Attachments and artifacts:
- traces/coalesce-run-2026-05-12.nsys-rep (raw Nsight capture)
- traces/attn-microbench-offsets-2026-05-14.csv (in-progress microbench results)
- perf/heap-dump-2026-05-13.txt (allocation timeline around layout conversion)

Action items (short):
- Aisha: push revert hotfix for production branch and roll to staging (2026-05-19).
- Miguel: run microbench matrix and upload CSV to traces/ (2026-05-20).
- Hannah: prototype 64-bit reduction and report bank_conflict counters (2026-05-22).
- Ethan: update autotuner heuristics to consider alignment penalties (2026-05-28).

Questions for the team:
- Do we want allocator-level alignment hints as an immediate interface (API vs implicit by tensor dtype)?
- Are there other places where blocked-by-16 layout was used that we should audit?

If you pick this up: start with attached nsys-rep and the microbench csv, repro on local A100 (or equivalent) and iterate on the microbench before touching production kernels.

-- end of notes --
